label: Rule of Blessings 1QSb (Serekh HaBerakhot) — Complete
summary_plain: The Rule of Blessings contains blessings to be spoken over members of the covenant community. The first blessing is for the faithful members of the covenant: may YHWH bless you from his holy habitation and open for you the eternal fountain. The second blessing is for the high priest: may YHWH lift his countenance upon you and make you holy among his people and set you as a crown of glory. The third blessing is for the sons of Tzadok, the priests: may YHWH bless you and keep you, may he renew the covenant of eternal priesthood for you. The fourth blessing is for the Prince of the Congregation (Nasi HaEdah): may YHWH raise you to everlasting heights and make you as a fortified tower.
summary_scholarly: 1QSb (Serekh HaBerakhot) was found appended to 1QS and 1QSa in Cave 1. It is a liturgical text containing a series of blessings structured hierarchically: the covenant community, the high priest, the priestly line, and the Prince of the Congregation (a royal-messianic figure). The blessings draw heavily on the Birkat Kohanim (priestly blessing) of Bamidbar 6:24-26 but expand it significantly. The blessing for the Prince of the Congregation (Col V) uses royal-messianic language: he strikes the earth with his mouth, he slays the wicked with the breath of his lips — language that echoes Yesha’yahu 11:4. The text preserves a liturgical theology in which YHWH’s blessing flows through established channels: community, priest, priesthood, prince.

key_terms.definition: Rule of Blessings — 1QSb, appended to 1QS and 1QSa in the same Cave 1 scroll. Contains a series of priestly blessings to be recited over the congregation, the high priest, the sons of Zadok (priests), and the Prince of the Congregation (the royal/messianic leader).

Prince of the Congregation — the royal/military messianic figure blessed in the final section of 1QSb. He is to judge the poor with righteousness, smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, destroy the wicked with the breath of his lips — language drawn from Yesha'yahu 11.

The priestly lineage that the Qumran community traced itself to — the legitimate Zadokite priests displaced from the Jerusalem Temple. 1QSb contains a specific blessing over the Sons of Zadok as the covenant's authorized priestly line.

The blessing in 1QSb over the high priestly figure: may YHWH lift up his face to you and give you peace. The form echoes the Aaronite blessing of Bamidbar 6:24-26 but is reworded and expanded for the covenant community's eschatological context.

The weapon of the Prince of the Congregation in 1QSb col.5, drawn from Yesha'yahu 11:4: he will smite the earth with the rod of his mouth and destroy the wicked with the breath of his lips. This is judgment-language, not military conquest — speech/decree as power.

In 1QSb, the angelic hosts alongside whom the high priest serves. The priestly blessing in 1QSb places the high priest in the dual-register context: he ministers with the holy ones (angels) in the heavenly-earthly assembly.

The blessing over the Prince of the Congregation in 1QSb col.5 is saturated with language from Yesha'yahu 11: a shoot from the stump of Yishai, the spirit of YHWH upon him, righteousness as the girdle of his loins, judgment of the poor. 1QSb uses these as the vocabulary of the eschatological royal blessing.

The 1QSb blessing over the Sons of Zadok invokes the covenant of eternal priesthood — YHWH's covenant with Pinehas and the legitimate priestly line. The Qumran community saw themselves as the true inheritors of this covenant against the corrupted Jerusalem priesthood.

The cave and scroll designation for the Rule of Blessings — the 'b' suffix indicates it is the third document in the same Cave 1 scroll as 1QS and 1QSa. The scroll contained these three texts together as a governing triad.

The blessings in 1QSb are framed for 'the end of days' — not current priestly service but the perfected messianic-age service. They envision the ideal functioning of the covenant's priestly and royal offices after YHWH's visitation.

faq.question: What is 1QSb (Rule of Blessings)?
faq.answer: 1QSb is the third document appended to the Cave 1 scroll that also contains 1QS (Community Rule) and 1QSa (Rule of the Congregation). It contains a series of priestly blessings for the end of days: blessings over the congregation, the high priest, the Sons of Zadok (the community's priestly lineage), and the Prince of the Congregation (the royal/messianic leader). These blessings are not for current use but for the perfected eschatological age.

faq.question: Who is the Prince of the Congregation in 1QSb?
faq.answer: The Prince of the Congregation (Nesi HaEdah) is the royal/military messianic figure in Qumran texts — the Messiah of Yisra'el, distinct from the priestly Messiah of Aaron. The 1QSb blessing over him is saturated with Yesha'yahu 11 language: a shoot from Yishai, the spirit of YHWH, judgment of the poor, smiting the earth with the rod of his mouth, destroying the wicked with the breath of his lips. His authority is expressed through righteous judgment and divine decree, not simply military force.

faq.question: How does 1QSb use Yesha'yahu 11?
faq.answer: The blessing over the Prince of the Congregation in 1QSb col.5 draws directly on Yesha'yahu 11's portrait of the ideal Davidic ruler: wisdom and understanding, the fear of YHWH, judging the poor with righteousness, the rod of his mouth as his weapon, the breath of his lips as destruction of the wicked. 1QSb applies this prophetic portrait to the community's eschatological royal figure. The DSS treated Yesha'yahu 11 as a source text for messianic expectation — the NT borrowed this same passage later.

faq.question: What is the Aaronite blessing connection in 1QSb?
faq.answer: The high priestly blessing in 1QSb echoes the Aaronite blessing of Bamidbar 6:24-26 — the three-fold blessing of YHWH lifting his face, giving grace, and giving peace. 1QSb uses this ancient form but recontextualizes it for the covenant community's eschatological high priest who ministers with the angels of the presence. The community read themselves as the true inheritors of the Aaronite blessing's meaning.

faq.question: What is the significance of the Sons of Zadok?
faq.answer: The Sons of Zadok were the legitimate priestly lineage according to the Qumran community — descended from Zadok, Dawid's priest, whose line is promised in Yekhezkel 44 as the legitimate priests of the future Temple. The community believed the Jerusalem Temple's priesthood had become illegitimate (whether through the Hasmonean takeover of the high priesthood or earlier corruption). By identifying themselves as the Sons of Zadok, they claimed the mantle of legitimate priestly authority that the Temple had forfeited.

faq.question: Why is 1QSb framed for the end of days rather than current use?
faq.answer: Because the community's ideal priestly and royal leadership was not present in its current form. The legitimate high priest and the messianic Prince had not yet arrived. 1QSb preserved the ideal form of blessing that would be used when the proper leadership was established — a document of anticipation. Like 1QSa's messianic banquet, 1QSb's blessings define what the perfected covenant community will look like, shaping present practice by its eschatological goal.

faq.question: How does 1QSb fit with 1QS and 1QSa?
faq.answer: The three documents form a triad on the same Cave 1 scroll: 1QS governs current community life (entry, Two Spirits, penal code, Maskil's hymn); 1QSa governs the eschatological assembly at the end of days; 1QSb provides the liturgical blessings for the eschatological leadership at that same end of days. Together they move from present practice (1QS) to future assembly structure (1QSa) to future blessing liturgy (1QSb). The whole scroll is a complete governing vision from present to eschatological.

faq.question: What does the 'rod of his mouth' mean?
faq.answer: The rod of his mouth (Yesha'yahu 11:4, cited in 1QSb) is a figure of speech for authoritative decree — the Prince of the Congregation's judgment-speech functions as a rod, smiting the earth by its pronouncement. This is not literal weapon imagery but prophetic judgment language: his word has the force of execution. This contrasts with the War Scroll's military imagery — in 1QSb, the Prince's power is expressed through righteous speech, not just armies. The NT's Revelation 19:15 borrows this same imagery, applying it to its invented figure.

faq.question: What connects 1QSb to the Songs of Sabbath Sacrifice (Shirot)?
faq.answer: Both texts place the community in the same dual-register frame: the earthly covenant community worshipping alongside the angelic heavenly assembly. 1QSb's blessing over the high priest says he ministers 'with the angels of the presence' — the same holy ones who populate the heavenly temple in the Shirot. This shared framework means the community's earthly priestly service is simultaneously a participation in the heavenly temple's ongoing angelic service.

faq.question: How does 1QSb understand priestly authority?
faq.answer: Priestly authority in 1QSb is covenantal and lineage-based: it rests on the Sons of Zadok's descent from the legitimate priestly line and on YHWH's covenant with Pinehas (eternal priesthood). It is not institutional — the Jerusalem Temple's official priesthood had forfeited this authority by corruption. The community held the authentic covenant, the authentic lineage (or identified with it), and the authentic liturgy. The blessings of 1QSb articulate what that authentic priesthood looks like when properly constituted.
